cards.front: Recall a key point about Composition and Layout
cards.back: Composition is the arrangement of visual elements within the picture plane — it guides the viewer's eye and creates meaning.

cards.front: Recall a key point about Composition and Layout
cards.back: The rule of thirds divides the image into nine sections; placing focal points at intersections creates dynamic balance.

cards.front: Recall a key point about Composition and Layout
cards.back: Negative space (the empty areas) is as important as positive space — it defines shapes and creates breathing room.

cards.front: Recall a key point about Composition and Layout
cards.back: Foreground, middle ground and background create depth and lead the viewer into the picture.

cards.front: What should you know about fine art exam tips?
cards.back: Create thumbnail sketches showing alternative compositions for the same subject. Annotate each explaining why you chose the final arrangement. Show understanding of how composition affects mood and meaning.

Students often make mistakes with this topic. Wrong: A good composition always centres the subject for symmetry. Correct: Centred compositions can feel static. Off-centre placement (rule of thirds), asymmetrical balance and unusual cropping often create more dynamic, engaging compositions.

Compare the compositions of two paintings from different periods. Analyse how each artist has arranged elements to create balance, focus and meaning. How has this influenced your own compositional decisions?
